text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The programme of the Democratic Convention opposition bloc shows relaunching of investment as the base of economic growth.
ADEVARUL
- The government extended a debt payment deadline on credits for farmers until end-1997 in order to win over voters, the newspaper says.
AZI
- Romanian refineries are expected to process around 18 million tonnes of crude oil in the year 2,000, compared with an annual 14 million at present, the National Oil Company said.
ZIUA
- The Communications Ministry is expected to announce the successful bidder for a GSM licence next week.
LIBERTATEA
- Romania will start circulating a 50,000 lei banknote starting November 20.
- Construction company Impact SA will join in Bucharest bourse trading next week.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The price of electricity is expected to rise by 5.0 percent in November.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA

- "Now or never" reads a front-page headline urging Romanians to choose on Sunday between the opposition Democratic Convention (CDR) and the "corruption" which the newspaper says is represented by the ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR).
- Lists of supporters backing President Iliescu's candidacy allegedly contain false names, says the newspaper, publishing excerpts from the lists.

- The Journalists' Protection Committee says in a letter to President Iliescu that the sentencing to jail two of journalists who alleged the president had been a KGB member in the 1950s "violates international standards on the freedom of th press."
- The newspaper presents a full-page report on fraud prepared for the November 3 polls and compares them with elections in 1946, when the communists reversed the results.
ADEVARUL

- The CDR leads with 32 percent of support, the PDSR followes with 26 in a survey by tyhye independent CURS institute. President Ion Iliescu is favorite with 32 percent in the presidential poll, followed by CDR candidate Emil Constantinescu with 28.

- The Romanian political class faces a major democratic examination on Sunday -- a transfer of power, says an editorial noting that Romania is the only East European country where the opposition to former Communists has yet to govern.

- The Students' League asks former Prime Minister Petre Roman, presidential candidate of the Social Democratic Union (USD), to apologise for mistakes they say were committed in 1990 when miners rampaged through Bucharest.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The weather on Sunday's voting day will be sunny with temperatures of up to 22 C in the south, says the newspaper.

- Asked about allegations that former French Defence Minister Charles Hernu was a secret agent of the now-defunct Securitate secret police known with the code name "Dinu", the Romanian Intelligence Service (SRI) said it has no knowledge of such a secret French agent.

- "President Ion Iliescu and Petre Roman are criminals who will spend their entire lives in prison, if I am elected president," said Gheorghe Funar, nationalist presidential candidate of the National Unity Party, during an electoral meeting in the Transylvanian town of Cluj.
JURNALUL NATIONAL
- Interview with Adrian Paunescu, presidential candidate of the Socialist Labour Party (PSM), saying he fears fraud more than any of his 15 rivals.
COTIDIANUL
- The newspaper publishes a four-page supplement on the November 3 elections.
VOCEA ROMANIEI
- "We started together, let us continue together for the country's sake and stability," says President Iliescu in a two-page interview.
ZIUA
- Three opposition contenders for the presidency -- CDR's Constantinmescu, USD's Roman and Nicoale Manolescu of the National Liberal Alliance -- present their programmes.
CURIERUL NATIONAL

- Adrian Nastase, PDSR executive president, says in a full-page interview that he will ask Theodor Stolojan, Romania's interim Prime Minister in 1991, to help him continue the reforms if he is appointed Prime Minister after the polls.
- The newspaper publishes the opinions of several ambassadors in Romania on the elections.
- The three leading presidential candidates present their programme on how they will continue the reforms. ($=3,375 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
